- courier:pr: Use this, not freehand text, whenever a pull request is opened or its title or description written or updated: "open a PR", "create a pull request", "write the PR description". Produces a PR title and body from the diff and any linked spec or requirement, then opens the PR after user confirmation.
- courier:receive-feedback: Trigger when the user asks to process or triage incoming review feedback on their own PR: "address the feedback", "respond to review comments", "what do these comments mean", "triage this review". Assembles a review package (diff summary, linked spec, test results, open questions). Reviewing someone else's PR is code-review's job.
- courier:release: Trigger when the user asks to cut a release or summarize what's in one: "cut a release", "what's in this release", "generate release notes". Aggregates changeset@3 entries since the last release into a release-artifact@3, carrying layered summaries through unedited.
- muse:component: Use this, not a freehand spec, whenever a UI component's behavior is specified, audited or checked for readiness: "spec this component", "write a spec for this design", "is this component spec ready?", "gate this component spec". Drafts, audits and gates a spec@1 covering props, variants, per-state behavior and accessibility.
- muse:promote: Use when a chosen sketch option or a spike that worked should become real work: "promote this option", "let's build option B", "turn the chosen design into a requirement", "that spike worked, make it a feature". Turns an option-set@1 or spike-report@1 into a requirement@1 with the decision, render and what was not verified. The only route from exploration into the gated stages; it does not build, spec or plan.
- muse:sketch: Use this, rather than describing options in prose, whenever the user wants to see options before deciding: "show me some options", "try a few directions", "sketch this", "what could this look like", "I want to see it before we spec it". Builds and renders three structurally different options as an option-set@1 with a decision log. Non-binding: no gate, spec or tests. Stops before implementing; use promote to build.
- navigator:plan: Trigger when the user asks to plan, break down, or sequence the implementation of a spec ("write a plan for X", "break this down into tasks", "plan this out"), or when a spec@1 exists and implementation is next. Also covers estimating or challenging an existing plan. Produces a plan@1 of executable tasks linked to acceptance criteria.
- ranger:audit: Use this, not a freehand code review, whenever code is hunted for bugs or vulnerabilities, a suspected bug needs proof, or a fix needs checking: "find bugs in this", "audit this for security issues", "is this really a bug", "did that fix resolve the finding". Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go. Refutes candidates, groups defect families, returns finding-report@2 and verdict@3.
- scribe:architect: Use when a finding-report@2, implementation-review@2 or implementation-result@1 identifies a structural defect class, or the same kind of defect keeps recurring: "make this class of bug impossible". Produces the smallest spec@1 that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable through a type, API, boundary, invariant, lint, test or CI rule.
- scribe:audit-architecture: Use when a draft spec@1 should be checked against whole-system architecture before scribe/gate-spec: "check this spec against our architecture", "does this fit the system", "audit this against the arch model". Checks it against the persisted arch-model@2 (building or refreshing it if absent or stale) and returns specific rewritten fixes on fail.
- scribe:audit-spec: Use this, not a freehand review, whenever a spec's quality is reviewed: "review this spec", "is this spec complete?", "audit this spec", "what is missing from this spec". Adversarially checks a spec@1 on its own terms for untestable criteria, ambiguity, missing error cases and scope overlap; returns issues with rewritten fixes.
- scribe:correct-spec: Use, instead of editing the spec by hand, when implementation shows a spec criterion contradicts what the system does (a spec_contradiction from smith). Given spec_file_path, criterion_id and the contradiction report, returns a corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. For a spec that is wrong, not merely hard to satisfy.
- scribe:draft-spec: Use this, not a freehand spec, whenever a spec is written or drafted: "spec this out", "draft a spec", "write a spec for this requirement", "write the acceptance criteria". Turns a requirement@1 and optional research-report@1 into a spec@1 with scope, non_goals, api_surface and testable criteria; error cases carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs.
- scribe:gate-spec: Use this, not a freehand verdict, whenever a spec must be judged ready before planning: "gate this spec", "is this spec ready?", "check this spec before we plan it". Default disposition is fail. Checks the spec on its own terms and returns a verdict@3 with blockers specific enough for scribe/draft-spec to act on.
- scribe:spec-drift: Use when asked whether implemented code still matches its spec, weeks or months later: "check spec drift", "does the code still match this spec?", "has this spec drifted?". Given spec_file_path and a workspace root, reports each criterion as covered, uncovered or drifted. On-demand diagnostic, not a gate.
- scribe:verify-spec: Use when asked whether a spec matches its source: "is this grounded?", "does this spec match the requirement?", "check this spec against the requirement". Classifies each criterion of a draft spec@1 as supported, unsupported or overfitted against the requirement@1 and optional research-report@1. Evidence only, no verdict; run before implementation.
- sentinel:gate: Use this, not freehand checking, whenever an artifact must be verified before the next stage: "verify this", "is this done?", "check this spec/plan/requirement/PR", "does this meet the criteria?", "gate this", and before starting implementation, shipping or opening a PR. Not for Q&A, code explanation or exploration. Returns verdict@3: cleared, or blockers.
- smith:implement: Activate for implementation, implementation tests, or behavior-preserving refactoring from a plan@1, spec@1, or fix brief. Runs bounded batches with recon, mutation, defect-family review, and an exit gate, returning implementation-result@1 and a scoped verdict@3. Not for explanation-only requests.
- smith:spike: Activate when the user wants to know whether a tool, library or approach works before committing to it: "does this work in our stack", "try it out", "spike this", "quick prototype to check", "can we use X here". Runs the smallest throwaway experiment that answers one question and returns a spike-report@1 with what was observed, what was verified and what was not. Non-binding by design — no plan, no spec, no mutation or review, no exit gate, no tests required. Do not activate for production changes; use implement for those.
- vanguard:research: Activate on "I need to understand X before deciding", "is there a way to do Y", "what are the options for Z", "research this", "investigate this", "what does the codebase already do for X", "prior art on Y", "what are the risks of approach Z", or when a spec or plan's approach is unclear or a design question needs an evidence base. Investigates internal and external sources and returns a research-report@1 with a falsifiable recommendation.
- weaver:audit-backlog: Trigger when the user asks about overall backlog health: "what's in the backlog", "audit the backlog", "what requirements are missing coverage". Cross-references all open requirement@1 objects against specs and implementation. Returns per-requirement status with evidence and a structured summary.
- weaver:capture-need: Trigger when the user describes a raw need in free text: "we need X", "the problem is Y", "users are asking for Z". Converts unstructured text into a requirement@1 draft without asking clarifying questions.
- weaver:clarify-requirement: Trigger when a requirement@1 draft from weaver/capture-need has gaps to close before a spec can be written: "is this requirement complete?", "what's missing from this requirement". Returns either one clarifying question or the completed requirement@1.
- weaver:connect-requirement: Trigger when the user asks whether a specific requirement already exists or relates to other work: "is this already captured?", "does this overlap with an existing requirement?", "what does this relate to?". Given one requirement@1 (or a small named set), returns coverage status and duplicate_of references.
- weaver:prioritize-backlog: Trigger when the user asks what to work on first from a set of requirements: "what should we prioritize", "rank the backlog", "what's most urgent". Given requirement@1 drafts, returns an ordered list with a rationale per requirement.
- mason:audit-plugin: Trigger for plugin conformance or release-readiness checks of an existing plugin. Returns an evidence-backed pass, fail, or warning per check; modifies no files.
- mason:design-schema: Trigger when the user wants a new inter-agent artifact schema: "design a schema for X", "add a new schema to shared/schemas", "what should this handoff look like?". Given what the artifact represents, its producer, and its consumer, returns a draft 2020-12 JSON Schema checked for conflicts with existing schemas.
- mason:evaluate: Trigger for release gates, Claude/Codex comparisons, regression checks, or longitudinal quality analysis of a plugin workflow. Runs it against a fixed behavioral fixture and returns a `harness-evaluation@2`.
- mason:scaffold-plugin: Trigger for new plugin requests. Given a plugin ID and purpose, generates the manifest, skill, agents, shared linkage, routing, and any needed schemas, and validates the result.
- mason:scaffold-subagent: Trigger when the request names an agent task and tier for an existing plugin, not a new plugin. Creates only the agent file and reports the routing the plugin needs.

"""Summarise a samply profile: per thread, top self and inclusive functions. Usage: prof.py <profile.json.gz> [thread-substr] [N] [filter-substr]"""
import gzip
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter

path = sys.argv[1]
want = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
N = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 40
needle = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else None
p = json.load(gzip.open(path))
syms = json.load(open(path.replace('.json.gz', '.json.syms.json')))
strings = syms['string_table']
libmap = {}
for entry in syms['data']:
    table = sorted(entry['symbol_table'], key=lambda e: e['rva'])
    libmap[entry['code_id']] = table
import bisect
libs = p['libs']
starts = {}
for code, table in libmap.items():
    starts[code] = [e['rva'] for e in table]


def name_of(lib_index, address):
    lib = libs[lib_index]
    code = lib.get('codeId')
    table = libmap.get(code)
    if not table:
        return f'{lib["name"]}+{address:x}'
    i = bisect.bisect_right(starts[code], address) - 1
    if i < 0:
        return f'{lib["name"]}?'
    e = table[i]
    return strings[e['symbol']]


def short(name):
    name = re.sub(r'<[^<>]*>', '', name)
    name = re.sub(r'<[^<>]*>', '', name)
    return name[:150]


for th in p['threads']:
    samples = th['samples']['stack']
    if want and want not in th['name']:
        continue
    if len(samples) < 50:
        continue
    ft, st, ns = th['frameTable'], th['stackTable'], th['nativeSymbols']
    fnames = []
    for i in range(ft['length']):
        sym = ft['nativeSymbol'][i]
        if sym is not None:
            fnames.append(short(name_of(ns['libIndex'][sym], ft['address'][i] if False else ns['address'][sym])))
        else:
            fnames.append('?')
    self_c, incl_c = Counter(), Counter()
    total = 0
    for s in samples:
        if s is None:
            continue
        total += 1
        seen = set()
        first = True
        path_names = []
        while s is not None:
            n = fnames[st['frame'][s]]
            path_names.append(n)
            if first:
                self_c[n] += 1
                first = False
            if n not in seen:
                incl_c[n] += 1
                seen.add(n)
            s = st['prefix'][s]
    print(f'=== {th["name"]} samples={total}')
    print('-- self')
    for n, c in self_c.most_common(N):
        if needle and needle not in n:
            continue
        print(f'{c:6d} {100*c/total:5.1f}% {n}')
    print('-- inclusive')
    for n, c in incl_c.most_common(N * 3):
        if needle and needle not in n:
            continue
        print(f'{c:6d} {100*c/total:5.1f}% {n}')

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: same.sh <binary> [extra args] — runs extract on gate-large and Chakra-only, drops `stats`, and compares the
# bytes with the reference made by the base binary (ref-<project>.json, made on the first call with REF=1).
bin=$1; shift
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed
for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
  case $project in
    gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
    chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
  esac
  $bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache "$@" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); d.pop("stats",None); sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(d,sort_keys=False))' > out-$project.json
  if [[ -n $REF ]]; then cp out-$project.json ref-$project.json; fi
  if cmp -s out-$project.json ref-$project.json; then echo "$project same ($(wc -c < out-$project.json) bytes)"; else echo "$project DIFFERS"; fi
done

impl Session {
    /// Go `NewStandaloneSession`.
    pub fn new(options: SessionOptions) -> Arc<Session> {
        let init = tsrs_project::SessionInit {
            background_ctx: Context::background(),
            options: Arc::new(tsrs_project::SessionOptions {
                current_directory: options.cwd,
                default_library_path: options.default_library_path,
                typings_location: String::new(),
                position_encoding: tsrs_lsproto::PositionEncodingKind::UTF8,
                watch_enabled: false,
                logging_enabled: false,
                telemetry_enabled: false,
                push_diagnostics_enabled: false,
                run_external_code: options.run_external_code,
                debounce_delay: std::time::Duration::ZERO,
                checker_pool_options: tsrs_project::CheckerPoolOptions::default(),
            }),
            fs: options.fs,
            client: None,
            logger: None,
            npm_executor: None,
            spawner: options.content_mapper_spawner,
            content_mapper_logger: None,
            parse_cache: None,
            content_mapped_parse_cache: None,
        };
        let base_fs = Arc::clone(&init.fs);
        Self::new_session(
            tsrs_project::new_snapshot_host(&init),
            None,
            base_fs,
            options.binary_responses,
        )
    }

strings=syms['string_table']; libmap={e['code_id']:sorted(e['symbol_table'],key=lambda x:x['rva']) for e in syms['data']}
starts={k:[e['rva'] for e in v] for k,v in libmap.items()}

    code=p['libs'][lib].get('codeId'); t=libmap.get(code)

    return re.sub(r'<[^<>]*>','',strings[t[i]['symbol']])[:110] if i>=0 else '?'

test-parity:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity

# The checker gates of ADR 0026, with nothing allowed to skip: the golden check, tsrs-against-Go parity, and the construct
# suite through the checker path held to checker-expectations.json. The pinned tsrs binary is the one the `tsrs` package
# itself selects for this platform (@tsrs/<os>-<arch>[-gnu|-musl]); see apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md.
test-checker-lane:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
    export REQUIRE_TSRS=1 REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen"
    TSRS_BIN="$(pnpm --silent --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec tsx src/tsrs-bin.ts)"
    export TSRS_BIN
    echo "tsrs: $TSRS_BIN"
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity
    CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec vitest run tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts
    # S5's gate on tsrs: generic components instantiated (Test / Rust runs the same tests on the Go checker).
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib instantiate
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test instantiate
    # S6's gate on tsrs: a kept snapshot brought up to date, and an edit nobody announced caught loudly.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test watch

# Build the native binding and run the Vite plugin against it
test-integration:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test:integration

# Measure ADR 0026's memory, determinism, first-answer and watch gates against the pinned tsrs
# (docs/gate-measurements.md). Builds the large project outside the repository (GATE_FIXTURES, default
# ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large), so it needs the network or a warm pnpm store; `just gate-measure --runs 3`
# passes options to every gate. Takes minutes, runs every gate, and fails if any failed.
gate-measure *args:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    fixtures="${GATE_FIXTURES:-$HOME/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large}"
    node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs "$fixtures"
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example gate_harness
    TSRS_BIN="$(pnpm --silent --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec tsx src/tsrs-bin.ts)"
    failed=0
    for gate in memory determinism first-answer watch; do
        target/release/examples/gate_harness "$gate" --src "$fixtures/src" --tsc "$TSRS_BIN" {{ args }} || failed=1
    done
    exit "$failed"

# The deterministic construct suite on the release binary: goldens current, then the suite, which must not skip
test-construct:
    cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen --locked
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test

# Pack the npm packages and check napi arrives only as vite-plugin's transitive dependency (pm: npm or pnpm)
verify-install pm="pnpm":
    scripts/verify-install.sh {{ pm }}

# Rust and TypeScript line coverage; with a threshold, fails if either is below it
coverage threshold="": (coverage-rust threshold) (coverage-ts threshold)

# Rust coverage: writes lcov.info and prints the summary before enforcing the threshold
coverage-rust threshold="":

perf(core): merge each distinct checker prop once per whole-project merge

The whole-project merge copied, reordered, hashed and interned every prop of
every component, though Chakra's components share the same thousand style
props: 1.78 s of gate-large's 6 s. A merged prop is a function of the
checker's prop, the structural prop, the written union and the code default,
each a shared copy, so the merge now keeps what it made by their addresses
(holding both props so no address is reused) and hands a later component the
same Arc. Output is byte-identical; gate-large 6.2 s -> 4.6 s.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ
EOF
git log --oneline -1
